tool.name: Clank – AI Studio
tool.description: AI studio: chats with projects and templates, folders and repositories, images, music, video, group chat, documents and schedules.
tool.long_description: Works with the assistants connected in OmniWrench (options > AI assistants) and shares chats and projects with the chat panel. Every project gets its own workspace: local folders, Git repositories and online repositories (GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps – read online or cloned locally). Assistants can list, search and read the workspace, see Git status, log and diffs, propose file changes (shown as a diff) and run commands (shown with an explanation) – both only after confirmation, with an option to remember the answer for the session. What assistants may see is set on the page 'AI access' like for every tool; pseudonymization replaces addresses and names before sending. Files open in a viewer with highlighting and can be attached to the chat. The "Images" tab creates images with the connected image providers (OpenAI, Gemini, xAI, Black Forest Labs, fal.ai, Replicate, Stability AI, Ideogram, Recraft, MiniMax), optionally with reference images; the gallery shows the images of the AI data storage. In the "Group chat" several assistants discuss a topic in turn – with brakes for rounds, contributions, length, time and tokens, pause per round, stop on agreement or repetition, interjections and a summary. The "Music" and "Video" tabs create tracks and clips (Gemini Lyria/Omni Flash, ElevenLabs, MiniMax, Stability, Mureka, xAI, Runway, Luma, Seedance, fal.ai, Replicate and more), play them and edit them with ffmpeg: trim, convert to MP3 or GIF, add music to a video, remove sound, save a still. On Windows Clank downloads ffmpeg on request. Plus: templates for recurring questions (with placeholders), screenshots straight into the chat, documents written with the assistant and exported as HTML, PDF or ODT, and schedules that ask the assistant questions at fixed times.

grp.title: Group chat
grp.no_bot: No assistant is connected for the group chat yet. Set up connections under Options > AI assistants.
grp.intro: Several assistants discuss a topic in turn. Set participants, topic and brakes, then start. While it runs you can interject or pause at any time.
grp.col.name: Name
grp.topic_hint: What is it about? e.g. "Plan the migration of the clients to Windows 12 – risks and order."

grp.privacy: There are no function calls: the assistants only see the topic, your interjections and the contributions of the others. Pseudonymization follows this tool's "AI access" setting (addresses and names are replaced before sending). Group chats are stored like chats and encrypted if configured.

plan.info: Schedules ask the assistant a question at fixed times, e.g. "Every Monday, summarize the DHCP findings". Each run becomes a new chat. They run while OmniWrench is open with Clank; missed runs can be caught up the next time it opens. Functions that change something are never executed in scheduled runs.

mcp.title: MCP
mcp.intro: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) connects AI programs with tools. At the top, external MCP servers can be connected so that the assistants can use their tools. At the bottom, OmniWrench itself can be switched on as an MCP server for other AI programs (e.g. Claude Desktop, VS Code).
mcp.col.name: Name
mcp.client_hint: The tools are available to the assistants in KI-Studio and in the chat panel while KI-Studio is open. The AI access level of KI-Studio applies: read-only tools from level 3 (read), all others from level 4 and only after confirmation.
mcp.server_hint: The server is only reachable on this computer (127.0.0.1) and requires the token. It runs while KI-Studio is open. It offers the functions the built-in assistants have, with the same access levels and the same pseudonymization. A separate level for external programs can be set under "AI access" → exceptions → "MCP server". Changes are always confirmed here in the program.
mcp.name: Name:
mcp.stdio_warning: The command runs on this computer with the rights of the signed-in user. Only add servers from a trusted source.
mcp.trusted_tip: Without trust every tool counts as changing: it needs level 4 and a confirmation before each call.
mcp.tools_hint: Unchecked tools are not offered to the assistants.
mcp.confirm_call: Call tool "{tool}" of MCP server "{server}" with these values?
